Prompts, tokens & raw output

Fix provenance before expanding accepted labels

The app was exercised through Next/Previous, mask visibility, confidence filtering, two detector runs in the same view, a negative review, Undo, reload, and export. The first four scenes were reviewed through the student UI. Follow-up scenes C05–C14 were selected from the frozen original prediction snapshot, with no additional student-server writes. All independent GPT-6 Astra runs received clean source imagery and candidate coordinates; student classes and scores were withheld.

  1. Capture-date checks C01 reports 29 September 2022, while Esri zoom-18 metadata reports 31 January 2021. C04 reports 29 September 2022, while its candidate center reports 14 May 2022; the full crop includes 9 and 14 May. Store source tile coordinates, image hashes, and acquisition metadata with each prediction, and flag unresolved mismatches before review.
  2. The export button uses the wrong HTTP method. It sends POST and receives 405. The same endpoint supports GET and returns a downloadable GeoJSON; the six existing labels were successfully exported that way.
  3. Repeat detection adds duplicate outlines and leaves stale counts. The second identical-view run added two paths already present. After detection the review counter and confidence summary disagreed. A reload reconciled the starting 70 displayed entries / 12 reviewed to 64 unique predictions / 6 saved reviews.
  4. Separate appearance labels, geometry quality, and review status. Several proposals cross parcel boundaries; C01 is a non-field clearing in the current capture. The form lacks an uncertain or needs-split outcome. “Not burnt” was persisted as rejected while retaining the original positive model class. Preserve model output, but store a separate explicit review label and geometry decision.
  5. Make saving transactional. The served client marks a feature reviewed before save succeeds, and its save helper returns normally on HTTP errors. Code inspection indicates that a failed save can still advance the queue; this failure path was not injected into the live server.

Existing labels preserved: the temporary negative review was saved and verified, then undone after the date mismatch was found. Its newly created record was removed. All six original server labels were verified unchanged. None of these proposals was accepted into student ground truth.

Dataset expansion and evaluation protocol

Define the annotation unit first: whole field parcel or burn footprint. The new proposals use visible field parcels, plus one non-field confounder. Resolve mixed-date and mismatched-date cases before acceptance. Keep AI proposals distinct from expert-reviewed labels.

Sample missed parcels from raw imagery, high-confidence false positives, lower-confidence cases, model disagreements, and confusing soil/residue/shadow surfaces. Retain explicit negatives and uncertainty. Split evaluation by geographic scene and capture date so overlapping crops and neighboring parcels cannot leak across train and test sets. Use a fixed, independently adjudicated holdout before reporting accuracy; these selected cases are not an accuracy benchmark.

Recorded usage and limitations

No API key was used. Codex app-server ran GPT-6 Astra with high reasoning through the user’s subscription. Polygon checks establish valid geometry, not visual accuracy. No independent fire-event ground truth, thermal verification, or before/after analysis was obtained. Source imagery location error and model boundary error remain.
